title: Hand Hygiene: Technique, Timing, and Infection Prevention
content:
Hand hygiene is widely recognized as the single most effective intervention to stop the transmission of infectious pathogens, including bacteria, respiratory viruses, and gastrointestinal illnesses. Practicing clean hands reduces respiratory illnesses by up to 21% and diarrheal diseases by up to 40% in community settings.

Optimal 5-Step Handwashing Technique:
1. Wet: Wet your hands with clean, running water (warm or cold) and turn off the tap.
2. Lather: Apply adequate soap and rub hands together to build a rich lather. Be sure to lather the backs of your hands, between fingers, and beneath fingernails.
3. Scrub: Scrub your hands vigorously for at least 20 seconds (the time it takes to hum the 'Happy Birthday' song twice).
4. Rinse: Rinse your hands thoroughly under clean running water, ensuring all soap residue is washed away.
5. Dry: Dry hands completely using a clean single-use towel or an air dryer. Wet hands transfer germs much more readily than dry hands.

Alcohol-Based Hand Sanitizers:
When soap and water are not immediately accessible, use an alcohol-based hand sanitizer containing at least 60% alcohol. Apply enough sanitizer to coat all surfaces of both hands and rub together continuously until completely dry (about 20 seconds). Note that hand sanitizers do not remove grease, heavy soil, or certain resilient pathogens such as Norovirus or Clostridioides difficile.
